items.html:
A tall, athletic fast-medium bowler, Henry Osinde was born and raised in Uganda. He was first introduced to the game at the age of 15, but did not take it seriously until he was 17 and a student at Makerere University. He emigrated to Canada in 2000 and made history in 2002 by becoming the first African to play in the Toronto & District Cricket Association league. He soon made an impression in Canadian cricket, rising to the position of captain of Brampton Masters in the domestic club leagues. He made his Canada debut against, of all teams, Uganda in the ICC Trophy in 2005 and played some Intercontinental Cup cricket as well before his full ODI debut against Zimbabwe at Port of Spain in May 2006. He went wicketless at the World Cup in 2007 but has since distinguished himself as a strike bowler of considerable pace and skill and a matchwinner at Associate level. His record was somewhat marred, however, when he was sent home from Sri Lanka, where the national team had been preparing for the World Twenty20 Qualifiers in United Arab Emirates, for allegedly breaching the code of conduct in early 2010.
Liam Brickhill August 2010

stories.subTitle: Canada v Kenya, Group A, World Cup 2011, Delhi
stories.seoTitle: Canada v Kenya: Canada coast to win in basement battle
stories.summary: Canada won only their second World Cup match in four tournaments, beating Kenya in a low-profile, low-scoring scrap, and walked away from the Feroz Shah Kotlawith with bragging rights

stories.title: Canada fight back in tense chase
stories.subTitle: Canada v Ireland, ICC Intercontinental Cup, Toronto, 3rd day
stories.seoTitle: Canada v Ireland: Canada fight back in tense chase
stories.summary: A fighting 121-run stand for the ninth wicket, a probing opening spell and a late run-out helped Canada dominate much of the third day in a game in which the advantage has swung from one side to the other.

stories.title: Canada stare defeat despite Osinde, Surkari heroics
stories.subTitle: Canada v Ireland, ICC Intercontinental Cup, Toronto, 2nd day
stories.seoTitle: Canada v Ireland: Canada stare defeat despite Osinde, Surkari heroics
stories.summary: A five-wicket haul by Henry Osinde and a strong second-innings start anchored by Zubin Sukari helped Canada dominate most of the second day in Toronto, but Ireland struck towards the end to reclaim control
